proposals.relationship: Brown credits his reading and exchanges with Mary Douglas with helping him interpret religion within distinctive social worlds.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2003 lecture:2–3 and 9 explicitly corrects a seminar-based transmission story: an electrifying 1968 tea was followed by reading Purity and Danger privately and the Natural Symbols manuscript while travelling. The later account of British social anthropology at 12–14 retains the limits of explaining holiness from outside. This is a concrete reading and conversational debt, not formal seminar attendance, exclusive formation, or fresh reading of Douglas’s books. The existing anthropology influence remains intact.

proposals.relationship: Brown acknowledges Foucault’s friendship and writings as resources for his work on the self and sexual renunciation, while giving Hadot intellectual priority.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2003:2–3 describes the late 1980 Augustine/Cassian conversation and later informal encounters rather than seminars. At 13–14 Brown credits Hadot first, explains that Hadot drew him toward Foucault’s Care of the Self, and distinguishes their approaches. Own 2022:255/note 12 positively uses Les aveux de la chair, published posthumously in 2018, in reconsidering virginity as a bid for freedom. The later work cannot explain the 1988 book. Hadot’s stronger explicit debt is held for a missing endpoint; Foucault’s books and Brown’s complete memoir remain unread. The 2024 interview’s editorial Foucault claim is not treated as Brown’s own answer.
